evidence: The original `workspaceHasGitRemote` did `if err != nil { return false }`, so an unreadable remote list was indistinguishable from no remote; 39767f4 splits it into (bool, error). The fix routes the error to `recordReceiveError`, which the round-2 summary shows writes only to the automation trace, so the 'loud' channel the reply claims is silent in ordinary CLI runs.
guidance_note: When surfacing a swallowed error, check that the channel you route it to is visible in a normal run (stderr), not only in an opt-in trace, before calling it loud.

evidence: The hunk shows `if refsErr == nil && !hasRefs { return skipped }`, with refsErr then dropped and execution falling through to the fetch. That is the same error-collapsed-into-a-normal-path pattern F1 fixed a few lines up, and the F1 fix in 39767f4 did not sweep it. The agent's reply notes that performSyncPush has the same pattern too.
guidance_note: When fixing one error collapsed into a normal path, grep the same function and its siblings for every other `err == nil && ...` or discarded-error guard and fix them in the same commit.

evidence: The hunk sets `traceReason := "automatic receive fast-forwarded from the configured git remote"` unconditionally after SyncReceive, whatever result.State is. The flag is a false positive: 39767f4 changed only workspaceHasGitRemote and its call site, and this trace code is the PR's original code.
guidance_note: When a trace or log message describes an outcome, derive it from the result value instead of hardcoding the happy path.

narrative: The PR added automatic inline receive. Round 0 flagged a git-remote read error collapsed into 'no remote'. The fix split the result but left the same collapse on RemoteHasRefs (F2), and round 1 also caught an unrelated hardcoded trace reason (F3), so round 1 would have happened anyway. Round 2's out-of-diff finding showed that recordReceiveError, the channel every fix routed errors into, is trace-only and silent in normal runs, which undercuts the 'loud' claims in the F1 and F2 replies.
guidance_observations: The agent noticed the same permissive pattern in performSyncPush and scoped it out without filing anything visible on the thread.
Every fix routed failures into recordReceiveError and called that loud without checking whether the trace is visible outside automation runs.

evidence: After the round-1 fix (9a89eec) gated IssueResolution with Settled/Provisional, ThreeWay still called `resolution.Provisional()` and exposed the result through a public `MergeResult.Export`, so the gate could be bypassed one level up. The agent's reply calls it 'the same misuse vector ... reopened at the export level'. That makes this an incomplete fix of the round-1 out-of-diff finding, which has no F id, so caused_by is null; 2743402, the flagged commit, only changed label merging.
guidance_note: When gating an unsafe value behind a typed accessor, follow every caller that unwraps it and gate the aggregate it flows into in the same fix.

evidence: ResolveIssue merges Prompt (shown in the hunk) and Lane, but the agent confirms that `issueProjectionFrom`, which drives issueEqual change detection, omitted both, so a Prompt-only or Lane-only edit reads as unchanged and is dropped. guidance_note: When adding a field to a field-aware resolver, add it to the change-detection projection that decides whether the resolver runs, and test a single-field edit end to end.

narrative: The PR built a pure three-way field resolver. Rounds 0 to 2 raised out-of-diff findings (delete handling, ungated provisional rows, label resurrection) that the agent handled in issue comments with sound reasoning, including a reasoned partial rejection on delete-vs-unchanged. Round 3's F1 reopened the round-1 provisional-row finding at the export level because the row-level gate was not carried up through ThreeWay; with that done the first time, round 3 would have found only F2. F2 was an original omission in the change-detection projection.
guidance_observations: Three of the five finding-bearing rounds were out-of-diff summary findings answered in issue comments, so the fix-caused link from the round-1 finding to F1 is invisible in the F-numbered threads.
The label fix in 2743402 checked the authoritative table path as well as the row view, which kept a cosmetic-only fix from shipping.

narrative: The PR added a linear-history reconcile. The reconcile-cleanup path took three passes, all from out-of-diff summary findings: 3f761de still only logged failures, c287f8b promoted rotation failure, and 91ce19b stopped assuming a fresh connection lands on the data branch. Each pass fixed only what the latest finding named. Each round also carried an inline finding on untouched original code, so no round is strictly avoidable.
guidance_observations: The first cleanup fix rested on an unverified premise ('a fresh connection always opens on the data branch') that a later round had to remove; an assumption a fix depends on should be asserted in code the first time.
F1 repeated #231's trace-only-failure gap two days later, so the lesson from the previous PR in the same epic was not carried forward.

narrative: The PR built the prose-merge agent surface. Most findings were out-of-diff and answered in issue comments: duplicate resolutions, JSON-mode contract, stale-resolution fingerprint. The round-3 fingerprint fix changed the --resolve token shape but left the help, usage, and error strings advertising the old ID:FIELD=TEXT form, which cost round 4. guidance_observations: When a fix changes a CLI input format, grep for every string that documents the old format before pushing.
The agent's round-3 comment admits that the guidance and docs claimed stale resolutions were rejected before the code did, a doc-ahead-of-code claim made in the original PR.

The agent split F3 sensibly, keeping the oracle independent and adding the comment, and pushed back on F4 with a concrete permissions argument.

evidence: The agent rejected the reviewer's 'reject nil concrete values in SetRetention' as a defensive second enforcer and made only the encoder panic. guidance_note: When replacing a helper, carry over every branch of the one you delete (here the '-' and untagged cases) or show why it is dead.

narrative: The PR sealed retention into a Live|Archived|Deleted sum and drew 14 findings over five rounds. Four chains were fix-caused. Twin predicates were aligned instead of collapsed (F1 to F4). Retention-race tests were added piecemeal over three passes (F2, F6, F12). A typed-nil gate went on the encoder instead of the mutator the reviewer suggested, until the next round forced it there (F7 to F8). A new IssueWireFields dropped the '-' and untagged handling of the helper it replaced (F9 to F11, F13, F14). Every finding in round 4 was fix-caused, so that round was avoidable.
guidance_observations: On F7 the agent rejected the reviewer's correct mutator-gate fix by citing no-defensive-null-guards, then adopted the same fix one round later citing the same law.
Test-coverage findings recurred because each fix added only the rows named in the finding instead of the full base/no-base by variant matrix.
The pushbacks (F3, F5) were well reasoned and tied to recorded epic decisions.

evidence: The agent cites `git ls-remote` showing refs/tags/v6, and notes that the review run producing this finding executed this same workflow with a successful checkout step. The reviewer's 'latest is v4' is a stale-knowledge claim.

Draft PRs do trigger opened and synchronize, but the file is a generated copy whose header forbids hand edits, and the agent states this repo's workflow produces no drafts. Upstream in the template is the right place for the change.

The agent pushed back on all three: one premise was wrong (checkout@v6 exists), and the other two belong in the template. The domain change itself drew no findings.
